name: Tsukiji Outer Market
desc: Street market left after the inner auctions moved to Toyosu. Tamagoyaki, sushi counters, knives and fruit. Go after 9:00 so wholesale buyers are done; many stalls wind down by mid-afternoon. Some shops close Sunday or Wednesday. Price: free to walk; snacks about ¥300–¥1,200.

name: Toyosu Uogashi Yokocho
desc: Public shop floor inside Toyosu Market: knives, dashi, tamagoyaki, souvenirs. Pair with teamLab Planets on the same train line. Observation decks for the wholesale floor are separate and timed. Price: shops free to browse; snacks and tools from a few hundred yen.

name: Ameya-yokocho
desc: Covered market between Ueno and Okachimachi: snacks, dry fish, cheap clothes, New Year extras. Loud, cash-friendly, easy with the zoo or science museum. 45–90 minutes is enough. Price: free to walk; street snacks about ¥200–¥800.

name: Tokyo Ramen Street
desc: Eight regional ramen shops under Tokyo Station, Yaesu side. Pick one bowl and leave; lunch queues are long. Indoor, useful on a wet day or before the Shinkansen. Price: most bowls about ¥900–¥1,500.

name: Tsukishima Monja Street
desc: Eighty-plus griddle shops; you mix and scrape monjayaki at the table. A 10-year-old can help cook. Go mid-afternoon to skip the dinner line. Price: about ¥1,000–¥2,000 per person.

name: Nakamise snacks
desc: The official approach to Senso-ji: ningyo-yaki, sembei, melon-pan. Walk, snack, do not sit down. Combine with the Asakusa lucky-gods loop. Price: street free; sweets about ¥200–¥600.

name: Kura Sushi Harajuku
desc: Conveyor-belt sushi with English tablet and a capsule-toy game after five plates. Flagship store, one stop from Meiji Jingu. Better than hunting a random sushi counter. Price: plates from about ¥145; a kid meal is usually under ¥2,000.

name: Yanaka Ginza snacks
desc: Short local shopping street: menchi-katsu, senbei, cats on the steps. Pair with the Yanaka seven-gods walk. Quieter than Ameyoko. Price: free to walk; snacks about ¥150–¥500.

name: Kiyoken shumai
desc: Yokohama’s railway shumai, sold at the station and eaten cold on the train. Not a sit-down meal. A 15-piece box is the classic souvenir. Price: old-style shumai about ¥740 for 15; shumai bento about ¥1,180.

name: Komachi-dori snacks
desc: Pedestrian street from Kamakura Station toward Hachimangu: shirasu, dove cookies, taiyaki. Do this instead of a sit-down lunch if the shrine rites are the point. Weekend queues. Price: street free; snacks about ¥300–¥900.
